shared_elements: carved stone monument with rounded top and broadly symmetrical vertical axis
horizontal banding or belt-like divisions across the surface
small rectangular panels filled with cross/grid hatching
schematic paired curved forms flanking a central element (handle-like/arm-like)
shallow linear surface decoration on unpolished stone
justification: Both are symmetrical, round-topped stone monuments whose decoration is organised in stacked horizontal zones around a central axis, with discs, belt-like bands, and small hatched/cross-filled panels — the paired curved forms flanking a central rectangular element in A loosely echo the flanking arms and central chest disc in B. The decisive difference is manner and dimension: A is a flat slab covered in thin, uniform incised outline drawing with a continuous framing border, while B is a bulky three-dimensional figure carved in low relief with modelled facial features and no framing device.
